slots.title: US close — Sept. 25, 2026
slots.body:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average led the major US benchmarks, up 0.9% to 51,828.62 (+478.64 points), while the S&P 500 rose 0.5% to 7,742.09 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.5% to 27,068.72.

The Russell 2000 barely moved, up 0.1% to 2,837.55.

The CBOE Volatility Index fell 5.1% to 14.87, from a prior close of 15.67, with an intraday range of 14.68 to 15.92.

At 12:30 ET, durable goods orders for August showed 0.0% month-over-month versus a -0.4% estimate; ex-defense orders rose 0.1% versus a -0.6% estimate; ex-transportation orders rose 0.3% versus a +0.6% estimate.

At 14:00 ET, Michigan consumer sentiment for September printed at 48.1 versus a 47.6 estimate and a prior 51.7.

The Atlanta Fed GDPNow reading for Q3 was updated to 5.0% versus a 5.1% estimate and a 5.1% prior, in a medium-impact release at 14:20 ET.

Among megacaps, Microsoft stood out with a +3.7% close at 516.17; Costco rose 2.9% to 922.76; Tesla fell 1.5% to 372.11; Oracle fell 1.8% to 137.08; Intel, among the most active names in the feed, fell 3.4% to 123.00.

Nasdaq sector averages split sharply: Consumer Defensive led at +3.1%, Technology averaged +0.6%, Energy +0.5%, while Communication Services averaged -0.8%, Consumer Cyclical -0.9%, and Real Estate -2.6%.

Overseas indexes in the feed were mixed versus the US gain: Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.3% to 66,364.20; Hong Kong’s Hang Seng fell 1.3% to 24,510.10; the FTSE 100 rose 0.1% to 10,695.25.

Oil-linked quotes weakened: Brent crude fell 2.1% to 104.32; the United States Oil Fund (USO) fell 3.1% to 148.33.

Gold futures rose 0.5% to 4,321.20; the Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund (UUP) slipped 0.2% to 28.62; Bitcoin USD was roughly flat at 84,036.48 (-0.1%).

The latest Treasury snapshot in the feed (dated 2026-09-23) showed the 10-year yield at 5.1% and a 2s10s spread of 0.26 percentage points.

Five IPOs and three SPACs submitted initial filings this week, in the U.S. IPO weekly recap.
